question: A boy passes through 3 checkpoints. At each checkpoint, the guard takes half of the apples in his basket and then gives him 2 apples back. After the 3rd checkpoint, the boy has 10 apples left. How many apples did he start with?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 52 apples.

GIVEN

• At each of 3 checkpoints: apples → (half of the apples) + 2. After the 3rd checkpoint: 10 apples. Find the starting number.

SOLUTION

• Work backwards. If x is the number before a checkpoint, then after it the boy has x/2 + 2, so x = 2 × (after − 2).

• Before the 3rd checkpoint: 2 × (10 − 2) = 16

• Before the 2nd checkpoint: 2 × (16 − 2) = 28

• Before the 1st checkpoint: 2 × (28 − 2) = 52

• Check: 52 → 26 + 2 = 28 → 14 + 2 = 16 → 8 + 2 = 10 ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse each step: subtract 2, then double. Repeat three times: 10 → 16 → 28 → 52.

NOTE

• Option 1 (47) is wrong: it gives 25.5, then 14.75, then 9.375, not 10. Option 3 (35) is wrong: it gives 19.5, then 11.75, then 7.875. Option 4 (45) is wrong: it gives 24.5, then 14.25, then 9.125. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

question: A man introduces a woman by saying, 'Her brother's father is my father's only son.' The man has no siblings. How is the woman related to the man?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Daughter.

GIVEN

• Man: "Her brother's father is my father's only son." The man has no siblings.

SOLUTION

• My father's only son = the man himself, because he has no siblings.

• So "her brother's father" = the man. Her brother is therefore the man's son.

• The woman is the sister of the man's son, so she is the man's daughter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• "My father's only son" = myself (when I have no brother). Then work outwards: her brother's father is me, so her brother is my son, and she is my daughter.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Sister) is wrong: the man has no siblings. Option 3 (Niece) is wrong: a niece is the child of a sibling, and he has none. Option 4 (Wife) is wrong: the woman is the sister of the man's son, not the man's wife.

question: In the following question, a matrix of numbers is given. These numbers follow a certain pattern either row-wise or column-wise. Identify this pattern and choose the missing number accordingly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 10.

GIVEN

• Matrix: Row 1: 18, 13, 8; Row 2: 16, 11, 6; Row 3: 14, 9, 4; Row 4: 20, 15, ?

SOLUTION

• In every row, the numbers decrease by 5 from left to right.

• Row 1: 18 − 5 = 13, 13 − 5 = 8 ✓. Row 2: 16 − 5 = 11, 11 − 5 = 6 ✓. Row 3: 14 − 5 = 9, 9 − 5 = 4 ✓.

• Row 4: 20 − 5 = 15, 15 − 5 = 10

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the difference between neighbouring numbers in the complete rows first; if it is constant (−5), apply it to the incomplete row.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2) is wrong: 15 − 2 = 13, not 5. Option 3 (8) is wrong: 15 − 8 = 7, not 5. Option 4 (18) is wrong: it is larger than 15, so the row would increase, not decrease by 5.

question:

3, 7, 13, 21, 31, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 43.

GIVEN

• Series: 3, 7, 13, 21, 31, ?

SOLUTION

• Differences: 7 − 3 = 4, 13 − 7 = 6, 21 − 13 = 8, 31 − 21 = 10. The differences increase by 2 each time, so the next difference is 12.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• When the differences themselves form an AP (4, 6, 8, 10, 12), it is a second-order series.

NOTE

• Option 1 (41) is wrong: it needs a difference of 10, which repeats the last difference. Option 3 (45) is wrong: it needs a difference of 14. Option 4 (47) is wrong: it needs a difference of 16.

question: The sum of five consecutive odd numbers is 145. What is the greatest of these numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 33.

GIVEN

• Five consecutive odd numbers add up to 145. Find the greatest.

SOLUTION

• The middle number of five consecutive numbers is their average: 145 ÷ 5 = 29.

• The numbers are 25, 27, 29, 31, 33.

• Check: 25 + 27 + 29 + 31 + 33 = 145 ✓

• Greatest number = 33

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Middle number = sum ÷ 5 = 29. Add 2 and then 2 again for the greatest: 29 + 4 = 33.

NOTE

• Option 1 (29) is wrong: it is the middle number (the average), not the greatest. Option 2 (31) is wrong: the numbers 23 to 31 add up to 135. Option 4 (35) is wrong: the numbers 27 to 35 add up to 155.

question: Which of the following years will have the same calendar as the year 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 2030.

GIVEN

• Find the year with the same calendar as 2019.

SOLUTION

• 2019 is an ordinary (non-leap) year, so the matching year must also be non-leap and start on the same weekday (Tuesday).

• Odd days: each ordinary year adds 1 odd day and each leap year adds 2.

• From 2019 to 2030: 2019 (1), 2020 (2), 2021 (1), 2022 (1), 2023 (1), 2024 (2), 2025 (1), 2026 (1), 2027 (1), 2028 (2), 2029 (1) = 14 odd days = 0 after mod 7.

• So 2030 starts on the same weekday as 2019, and both are ordinary years: 2030.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• For an ordinary year, the calendar repeats after 6, 11 or 12 years depending on where the leap years fall; counting odd days until the total is a multiple of 7 gives the answer (here 11 years later).

NOTE

• Option 1 (2026) is wrong: it starts on Thursday, while 2019 starts on Tuesday. Option 2 (2028) is wrong: it is a leap year, while 2019 is not. Option 4 (2032) is wrong: it is a leap year, while 2019 is not.

question: In a non-leap year, if 1 January is Friday, which of the following pairs of months will start on the same day of the week?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. February and November.

GIVEN

• Non-leap year; 1 January = Friday. Find the pair of months that begin on the same weekday.

SOLUTION

• Days between 1 January and the 1st of a month, taken mod 7 (Friday = 0):

• February: 31 days → 3 (Monday). November: 304 days → 304 = 43 × 7 + 3 → 3 (Monday). The same day: Monday.

• May: 120 days → 1 (Saturday); August: 212 days → 2 (Sunday). Different.

• April: 90 days → 6 (Thursday); October: 273 days → 0 (Friday). Different.

• June: 151 days → 4 (Tuesday); December: 334 days → 5 (Wednesday). Different.

• So February and November begin on the same day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• In a non-leap year, February and March always start on the same day, and so do February, March and November. Remember the groups: (Jan, Oct), (Feb, Mar, Nov), (Apr, Jul), (Sep, Dec), and May, June and August alone.

NOTE

• Option 2 (May and August) is wrong: May starts on Saturday and August on Sunday. Option 3 (April and October) is wrong: April starts on Thursday and October on Friday. Option 4 (June and December) is wrong: June starts on Tuesday and December on Wednesday.

question: At what time between 3 o'clock and 4 o'clock will the hands of a clock be at right angles for the first time after 3 o'clock?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 3:32 ⁸⁄₁₁.

GIVEN

• Find the time after 3 o'clock when the hands are next at 90° to each other, between 3 and 4 o'clock.

SOLUTION

• At 3:00 the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 3, so they are already 90° apart. The next time they are at right angles is when the minute hand is 90° ahead of the hour hand.

• At 3:00 the minute hand is 90° behind the hour hand. The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute on the hour hand. To be 90° ahead, it must gain 90° + 90° = 180°.

• Time needed = 180 ÷ 5.5 = 360/11 = 32 ⁸⁄₁₁ minutes

• Time = 3:32 ⁸⁄₁₁

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Formula for 90° (minute hand ahead): minutes past h = (5h + 15) × 12/11 = (15 + 15) × 12/11 = 360/11 = 32 ⁸⁄₁₁ minutes.

NOTE

• Option 1 (3:16 ⁴⁄₁₁) is wrong: at this time the hands coincide (0° apart). Option 2 (3:21 ⁹⁄₁₁) is wrong: at this time the hands are 30° apart. Option 4 (3:38 ²⁄₁₁) is wrong: at this time the hands are 120° apart.

question: If 'mother' is called 'sister', 'sister' is called 'daughter', 'daughter' is called 'wife', 'wife' is called 'aunt' and 'aunt' is called 'mother', then what will a woman call her female child?

question: In a certain code language, 'paper pen ink' is written as 'xa do li', 'ink book cover' is written as 'li ga me' and 'paper cover file' is written as 'xa me tu'. What is the code for 'book'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ga.

• paper pen ink = xa do li

• ink book cover = li ga me

• paper cover file = xa me tu

SOLUTION

• "paper" is common to statements 1 and 3, and the common code is xa, so paper = xa.

• "ink" is common to statements 1 and 2, and the common code is li, so ink = li.

• "cover" is common to statements 2 and 3, and the common code is me, so cover = me.

• In statement 2 (li ga me), the codes for ink (li) and cover (me) are known, so "book" = ga.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Use common words to find their codes, then the remaining code in the statement belongs to the remaining word.

NOTE

question: During office hours, a caller asks for the OTP sent to your phone, saying it is needed to update your bank salary account. What is the best decision?
option_1: Share the OTP because the caller knows your office details
option_2: Share only if the caller sounds genuine
option_3: Do not share the OTP and report the call as fraudulent
option_4: Ask a colleague whether you should share it
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Do not share the OTP and report the call as fraudulent.

GIVEN

• A caller asks for the OTP sent to your phone, saying it is needed to update your bank salary account. Choose the best decision.

SOLUTION

• An OTP (One-Time Password) is a private security code. Banks and genuine officials never ask for it over the phone.

• A caller asking for an OTP is trying to commit fraud (vishing). The correct response is to refuse and report the call.

• The best decision is: Do not share the OTP and report the call as fraudulent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• In situational judgement questions on cyber safety, choose the option that protects confidential information and reports the incident through the proper channel.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Share the OTP because the caller knows your office details) is wrong: fraudsters often collect office details to look genuine. Option 2 (Share only if the caller sounds genuine) is wrong: a convincing voice does not prove that the caller is genuine. Option 4 (Ask a colleague whether you should share it) is wrong: the OTP must never be shared with anyone, and asking a colleague only delays reporting the fraud.

• To report cyber fraud in India: call the cyber crime helpline 1930 or use cybercrime.gov.in.

question: Find the angle between the hour hand and minute hand at 08:00.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 120°.

GIVEN

• Time = 8:00. Find the angle between the hour and minute hands.

SOLUTION

• At 8:00 the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 8.

• Angle = 30° × 8 = 240° (the larger angle), so the smaller angle = 360° − 240° = 120°

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Each hour mark is 30° apart. At 8:00 there are 4 hour marks between 8 and 12 (on the shorter side), so 4 × 30° = 120°.

question: A man is twice as old as his wife. Five years ago, he was three times as old as her. What is the present age of the wife?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 10 years.

GIVEN

• Man = 2 × wife (now). Five years ago, man = 3 × wife. Find the wife's present age.

SOLUTION

• Let the wife's present age = x, so the man's present age = 2x.

• Five years ago: 2x − 5 = 3(x − 5)

• 2x − 5 = 3x − 15 → x = 10 years (the man is 20 years old)

• Check: five years ago the man was 15 and the wife was 5, and 15 = 3 × 5 ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Present age of the younger = (5 × (3 − 1)) ÷ (3 − 2) = 10 for the pattern "twice now, three times before 5 years".

NOTE

• Option 1 (9 years) is wrong: the man would be 18, and five years ago the ages would be 13 and 4, with 13 ≠ 3 × 4. Option 3 (11 years) is wrong: the ages five years ago would be 17 and 6, with 17 ≠ 3 × 6. Option 4 (12 years) is wrong: the ages five years ago would be 19 and 7, with 19 ≠ 3 × 7.

question: A is older than B by 5 years. Three years ago, the ratio of their ages was 7 : 5. What will be the ratio of their ages after 7 years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 11 : 9.

GIVEN

• A − B = 5 years. Three years ago, A : B = 7 : 5. Find A : B after 7 years.

SOLUTION

• Three years ago, let the ages be 7x and 5x. The difference stays the same: 7x − 5x = 5 → x = 2.5.

• Present ages: A = 7 × 2.5 + 3 = 20.5 years; B = 5 × 2.5 + 3 = 15.5 years.

• After 7 years: A = 27.5 and B = 22.5.

• Ratio = 27.5 : 22.5 = 55 : 45 = 11 : 9

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• The age difference is always 5. After 7 years the ages are 27.5 and 22.5; divide both by 2.5 to get 11 and 9.

NOTE

• Option 1 (9 : 7), Option 3 (13 : 11) and Option 4 (15 : 13) are wrong: for a difference of 5 years, the ratio 11 : 9 gives ages 27.5 and 22.5, whereas these ratios (9 : 7, 13 : 11 and 15 : 13) do not match the ages obtained.

• The ages are not whole numbers, but the question asks only for the ratio, which comes out exactly.

question: Choose the option that does NOT belong to the same class/group as the others.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 372.

GIVEN

• Four numbers: 176, 242, 308, 372.

SOLUTION

• 176 = 11 × 16, 242 = 11 × 22 and 308 = 11 × 28. All three are multiples of 11 (with the multipliers 16, 22 and 28 rising by 6 each time).

• 372 ÷ 11 = 33.8…, so 372 is not a multiple of 11 (the next term in the pattern would be 11 × 34 = 374).

• The odd one out is 372.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Divisibility test for 11: (sum of digits at odd places) − (sum of digits at even places) must be 0 or a multiple of 11. For 372: (3 + 2) − 7 = −2, which is not a multiple of 11.

NOTE

• Option 1 (176), Option 2 (242) and Option 3 (308) are not the odd ones, because each is divisible by 11. (The PDF shows Option 2 as a wrong selection.)

question: Sophia and Olivia are sisters. Ethan and Noah are brothers. Sophia’s daughter is Noah’s sister. What is Olivia’s relationship to Ethan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Aunt.

GIVEN

• Sophia and Olivia are sisters. Ethan and Noah are brothers. Sophia's daughter is Noah's sister.

SOLUTION

• Sophia's daughter is Noah's sister, so Sophia is the mother of Noah and his sister.

• Ethan is Noah's brother, so Ethan is also Sophia's child.

• Olivia is the sister of Sophia, who is Ethan's mother. So Olivia is Ethan's aunt (mother's sister).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Mother's sister = maternal aunt (मौसी).

NOTE

• Option 1 (Mother) is wrong: Sophia, not Olivia, is the mother. Option 2 (Grandmother) is wrong: Olivia belongs to the generation of Ethan's mother. Option 3 (Sister) is wrong: Olivia is the sister of Ethan's mother, not of Ethan.

question: If 2#4=12 and 3#5=20, then find 4#6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

NOTE

• Option 2 (32), Option 3 (34) and Option 4 (36) are wrong: they do not follow the rule (a + 1) × b, which gives exactly 30 for 4 # 6.

question: Where does the Indus River rise from?
option_2: Peaks of the Nanda Devi hills

• The Indus River rises in Tibet from the Bokhar Chu glacier near Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar, at a height of about 5,000 m. It enters India in Ladakh (Jammu and Kashmir region) and then flows through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

• Option 4 (Plains of the Punjab province) is wrong: the Indus is joined by the Punjab rivers in the plains, but it does not rise there.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• The Indus is about 2,880 km long. Its main tributaries are the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej (the Punjab rivers). The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) divides the use of its waters between India and Pakistan.

question: What is the standard shape of a basketball?

question: Which factor is responsible for maintaining Earth's orbit around the Sun without the planet drifting away into space?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gravitational force.

 

ANSWER

 

• Gravitational force.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• The Sun's gravitational pull acts on Earth as the centripetal force, which keeps Earth moving in a nearly circular (elliptical) orbit. Earth's motion balances this pull, so it neither falls into the Sun nor drifts away into space.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 1 (Atmospheric pressure) is wrong: it is the force of air on a surface, and it does not control the orbit of a planet in space.

 

• Option 3 (Ocean currents) is wrong: they move water within Earth's oceans and have no effect on Earth's orbit.

 

• Option 4 (Magnetic waves) is wrong: the Sun's and Earth's magnetic fields are much too weak to hold Earth in orbit.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• Newton's law of universal gravitation: F = G m₁ m₂ / r². Kepler's laws describe the motion of planets: the orbit is an ellipse with the Sun at one focus. Earth's orbital speed is about 29.8 km/s.

question: Which phenomenon explains the bending of light as it passes through Earth's atmosphere, affecting how celestial objects appear?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Refraction.

 

ANSWER

 

• Refraction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another of different density. Earth's atmosphere has layers of different density, so light from stars and the Sun bends as it enters, and celestial objects appear slightly displaced from their true positions.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 1 (Reflection) is wrong: it is the bouncing back of light from a surface, not its bending.

 

• Option 3 (Diffusion) is wrong: it is the spreading of particles or light in all directions, and it is not the bending of a light ray.

 

• Option 4 (Absorption) is wrong: it is the taking up of light energy by a medium, which does not bend the ray.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• Atmospheric refraction causes the twinkling of stars and makes the Sun visible about 2 minutes before it actually rises and about 2 minutes after it actually sets. Scattering of light causes the blue colour of the sky and the red colour of the sunrise and sunset.

question: What is the importance of using satellite technology in monitoring climate change and environmental degradation globally?
solution_text:

• Global observation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• Satellites orbit Earth and can observe large areas, including oceans, forests, ice caps and remote regions, repeatedly and over a long time. This gives scientists global observation data for tracking climate change, deforestation, sea level, glacier melt and pollution.

• Option 3 (Limited use) is wrong: satellites have wide uses in weather, agriculture, disaster management and the environment.

 

• Option 4 (No relevance) is wrong: satellite data is one of the main sources of information on climate change.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• India's ISRO runs the INSAT series (for weather and communication) and the Oceansat and Cartosat satellites (for ocean observation and mapping). Satellites for earth observation commonly use sun-synchronous polar orbits.

question: Regarding the "Great Acceleration" in the context of the Anthropocene, which indicator showed the most dramatic surge post-1950?
option_1: Total forest cover in the Northern Hemisphere.
option_2: Global primary energy use and atmospheric Carbon Dioxide concentration.
option_3: Deep-sea biodiversity in the Arctic Ocean.
option_4: The rate of volcanic eruptions along the Ring of Fire.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Global primary energy use and atmospheric Carbon Dioxide concentration..

 

ANSWER

 

• Global primary energy use and atmospheric Carbon Dioxide concentration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• The "Great Acceleration" refers to the sharp rise in human activity from about 1950, shown by trends such as population, economic output, energy use, fertiliser use and CO₂ levels. Global primary energy use and atmospheric CO₂ concentration both rose steeply after 1950, linked with the burning of fossil fuels.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 1 (Total forest cover in the Northern Hemisphere) is wrong: this is not a surge indicator of the Great Acceleration, and forest loss has been a concern globally.

 

• Option 3 (Deep-sea biodiversity in the Arctic Ocean) is wrong: this is not an indicator of the Great Acceleration.

 

• Option 4 (The rate of volcanic eruptions along the Ring of Fire) is wrong: eruptions are natural events and did not surge because of human activity after 1950.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• The Anthropocene is the proposed geological epoch dominated by human influence. The term was popularised by Nobel laureate Paul Crutzen in 2000. The Great Acceleration graphs were published by Will Steffen and colleagues in 2015.

question: Who is known for discovering the basic rules of inheritance through experiments on pea plants?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gregor Mendel.

 

ANSWER

 

• Gregor Mendel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• Gregor Johann Mendel, an Austrian monk, performed experiments on garden pea plants (*Pisum sativum*) in the 1850s and 1860s and discovered the basic laws of heredity: the Law of Dominance, the Law of Segregation and the Law of Independent Assortment. He is called the "Father of Genetics".

• Option 4 (Harold Urey) is wrong: he worked with Stanley Miller on the Miller-Urey experiment on the origin of life.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• Mendel published his results in 1866, but they were ignored until 1900, when Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns and Erich von Tschermak rediscovered them. A monohybrid cross in pea plants gives a 3 : 1 phenotypic ratio, and a dihybrid cross gives a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio.

question: The provision related to the admission or establishment of new States is in:

question: Which Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to the "Right to Freedom of Religion"?

question: The sum of two numbers is 1260. If the larger number is divided by the smaller number, the quotient is 8 and the remainder is 45. What is the difference between the two numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 990.

GIVEN

• Sum = 1260. Larger ÷ smaller gives quotient 8 and remainder 45. Find the difference.

SOLUTION

• Let the smaller number be S. Then the larger number = 8S + 45.

• S + (8S + 45) = 1260 → 9S = 1215 → S = 135

• Larger = 8 × 135 + 45 = 1125

• Difference = 1125 − 135 = 990

• Check: 135 + 1125 = 1260 ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Smaller = (sum − remainder) ÷ (quotient + 1) = (1260 − 45) ÷ 9 = 135. Larger = 1260 − 135 = 1125.

NOTE

question: If the number 48327*8 is divisible by 11, what is the smallest whole number that can replace “*”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 1.

GIVEN

• The number 48327*8 (7 digits) is divisible by 11. Find the smallest whole number that can replace *.

SOLUTION

• Divisibility rule of 11: (sum of digits at odd places) − (sum of digits at even places) must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

• Digits from the left: 4, 8, 3, 2, 7, *, 8

• Odd places (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th): 4 + 3 + 7 + 8 = 22

• Even places (2nd, 4th, 6th): 8 + 2 + * = 10 + *

• Difference = 22 − (10 + *) = 12 − *. This must be 0 or 11: 12 − * = 11 gives * = 1

• Check: 4832718 ÷ 11 = 439338 ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• For a 0–9 digit, 12 − * can only be 11 (since * = 12 is not a digit), so * = 1.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2) is wrong: the difference would be 10, which is not a multiple of 11. Option 3 (3) is wrong: the difference would be 9. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.) Option 4 (4) is wrong: the difference would be 8.

question: The third proportional to x and (x + 100) is 405. If x > 100, find the value of x.

• Check: (225)² ÷ 125 = 50625 ÷ 125 = 405 ✓

• Substitute the options: for x = 125, (225)² ÷ 125 = 405.

question: A train covers a fixed distance in 18 hours at a speed of 90 km/h. How much time will it take to cover the same distance at 120 km/h?

question: The average of 7 consecutive integers is 26. What is the largest integer?

question: A shopkeeper gives two successive discounts of 20% and 5% on an article. If the marked price is Rs. 2000, what is the total discount amount?

question: A student walks 3 km to school at 5 km/h and returns by the same route at 3 km/h. What is the total time taken for the round trip?

question: A wire is bent into the shape of an equilateral triangle with an area of 16√3 cm². If the same wire is bent into the form of a square, what will be the area of the square?

question: The area of a square S₁ is 256 sq. units. A second square S₂ is formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of S₁. A third square S₃ is formed by joining the midpoints of S₂, and so on. Find the perimeter of the fifth square (S₅) in the sequence.

In the following question, four sentences from a paragraph are provided. The sentences are jumbled and labeled A, B, C and D. Rearrange these sentences into the correct sequence to form a logically and grammatically coherent paragraph. From the given alternatives, select the option that represents the correct sequence.

 

A. But this is not true.

B. It is generally believed that the methodology of teaching learning is the concern of teachers only.

C. The teaching-learning methods are concerns of learners as well.

D. Learners have little or nothing to do with it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. BDAC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• B ("It is generally believed that the methodology of teaching learning is the concern of teachers only.") states the common belief and opens the paragraph.

 

• D ("Learners have little or nothing to do with it.") continues the belief, and "it" refers to the methodology in B.

 

• A ("But this is not true.") rejects that belief, and "this" refers to the belief in B and D.

 

• C ("The teaching-learning methods are concerns of learners as well.") gives the correct view.

◦ Correct order: B – D – A – C

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (BADC) is wrong: A ("But this is not true") would reject B before D has finished stating the belief, and C would then follow D, which contradicts the flow. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

 

• Option 2 (CADB) is wrong: C, which gives the corrected view, begins the paragraph, before the belief has been stated.

 

• Option 3 (ADCB) is wrong: A begins with "But this", which has no reference at the start.

 

NOTE

 

• Trick: look for contrast words such as "But" and for pronouns such as "this" and "it", which must come after the idea they refer to.

• Trick: arrange in time order (1750 → later club → 1909), and make sure "It" follows the noun it refers to.

question:
Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.

 

The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence into daily life has sparked a contentious debate regarding digital autonomy. Proponents argue that if developers (1)__ more robust ethical frameworks during the initial coding phase, the current issues with algorithmic bias would be less pervasive. solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. had implemented.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Blank (1): "Proponents argue that if developers ___ more robust ethical frameworks during the initial coding phase, the current issues … would be less pervasive." This is an unreal (imaginary) condition about the past with a result in the present (a mixed conditional): if + past perfect (had + V3), … would + base verb.

◦ Correct: …if developers had implemented more robust ethical frameworks…

 

• "Had implemented" is active and takes the object "more robust ethical frameworks".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: have implemented is wrong: the present perfect cannot be used in an "if" clause that expresses an unreal past condition. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

• Option 4: were implementing is wrong: the past continuous does not express the completed unreal past condition needed here.

 

NOTE

 

• Conditionals: Type 3 = if + had + V3, would have + V3 (past result). Mixed type = if + had + V3, would + V1 (present result).

question:
Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.

 

The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence into daily life has sparked a contentious debate regarding digital autonomy. Proponents argue that if developers (1)__ more robust ethical frameworks during the initial coding phase, the current issues with algorithmic bias would be less pervasive. Currently, a significant portion of the tech industry, including the most prominent software engineers, (2)__ that innovation must outpace regulation. This mindset, however, often leaves the public (3)__ to the whims of opaque data-harvesting practices. Furthermore, the (4)__ of digital surveillance in modern urban environments has led to a slow erosion of personal privacy. Only when transparency becomes the industry standard (5)____ to trust the systems that increasingly govern our lives.

 

Choose the most appropriate option for blank (5).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. will users begin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Blank (5): "Only when transparency becomes the industry standard ___ to trust the systems…" When a sentence begins with "Only when" (a restrictive adverbial), the main clause takes inversion: auxiliary verb + subject + main verb. The time reference is future, so the answer is will users begin.

◦ Correct: Only when transparency becomes the industry standard will users begin to trust the systems…

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: users will begin is wrong: it keeps the normal word order, but "Only when" requires inversion. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

 

• Option 3: users would begin is wrong: it has the normal word order and "would" does not match the present-tense clause "becomes".

 

• Option 4: did users begin is wrong: the past tense does not match the present-tense clause "becomes".

 

NOTE

 

• Rule: Only when / Only after / Only then / Not only / Hardly / Seldom + auxiliary + subject. Example: Only then did she realise her mistake.
